notes: Scope and protocol: only the assigned brief, scan009 packet and three scan009 source images were read. No other scan, reader return or witness batch was inspected. No delegation, OCR, recognition software, PDF text layer or external research was used. The whole image was viewed once for layout, half_a once and half_b once in that order, followed by each of the 20 recorded tight crops exactly once. No whole image or half was revisited, and no locus was recropped.

Coverage: every text block, every word and ending, the salutation and dateline, both marginal lines, the archive number, and every inline/display mathematical expression was compared with both C and H. Agreed readings were visually checked as well as disagreements. This includes all M/N/X/E/H occurrences, every index and exponent, both ordinals, parentheses, commas, equalities, inequalities, the crossed membership sign, both interval brackets, the low 2, the minus in the shift, all three arrows and the prime. This coverage statement is separate from mathematical proof checks.

Layout: this is a wholly handwritten letter page with a top-right dateline, Cher Deligne at upper left, one main block, a sideways two-line note in the left margin, a braced two-row formula and a triangle at the foot. The number 8 is a separate pencil archive number. There is no author page number, page total, signature, closing, letterhead or stamp visible on this page. The straight line near the lower paper edge is a page/reproduction boundary, not an independent authored drawing.

The main writing and the marginal writing are attributed only to unnamed pen hands. The page itself does not establish the writer’s personal identity. No handwritten wrappers are used around this entirely handwritten page. The paleness of part of the dateline is not treated as proof of a different person or a deliberate erasure.

The letter says the writer may be prevented by a leg from giving a first-cycle course in the first trimester, and may instead give a small algebra seminar concerning the fourbis of Mme Sinh, possibly transposed to the setting of champs. It calls the following consideration heuristique and says there should be a canonical distinguished triangle. These are the page’s tentative formulations, not a theorem certified by this transcription.

The marginal note concerns not finding the letter about Gr-Champs/Gr-champs cited by the recipient. Its first line is physically clipped through its upper portions. It has no insertion caret or independent marginal pointer. Its first line is therefore left uncertain even though its proposed words form a plausible sentence; the complete second line que tu cites is legible.

The dark numerical date 7.8.74 was clear in half_a. The faint mark before 7 does not establish a complete 2; the crop retains a possible foot-of-2 alternative after the stronger punctuation readings. H’s claims concerning another exemplar and a later verification are editorial assertions outside the assigned source image and were not imported as ink evidence.

The right edge cuts the end of cycl[e], most of the separate character read à, and part of the first-line portion of éventuellement. The first candidate cycl records the letters actually established before the edge. The other clipped readings retain doubt. The definite line continuation ment was joined to its preceding word, without supplying certainty to the lost internal letters.

The one clear correction consists of an older word overwritten by live Ext. Its old identity remains Hom/Ext; no additional complete old exponent is established. The live replacement has its own raised dotted i. The two layers are linearised in the TeX using deleted for the old word and live Ext for the final form; there is no insertion caret to reproduce. Other long curves under prose words are letter descenders, not separately drawn underlines.

Three small isolated points in mathematical contexts are explicitly recorded with uncertainty. One is raised after R, another is above the overwritten older middle letters, and a minute one is just inside the apex shift bracket. Their physical presence does not settle their textual status or attachment. A phantom alternative denotes a nontextual physical spot; it does not claim that the spot is absent. These low-confidence observations are intended for the main reader’s adjudication, not as certain new semantic notation.

The first comparison sign in the display was read from the parallel strokes as =. The neighbouring ≤ provides a local visual comparison, but the expected interval description was not used to normalise the first sign. The only mathematical check actually performed was the three-value substitution recorded in math_checks. No proof of the canonical triangle, the derived-functor description, or any general cohomological assertion was undertaken.

Witness differences settled from halves, with no crop made at this stage, are the paired straight quotation marks around champs (half_a), the resolution of tombe (half_a), the absence of a colon after canonique (half_b), and the physical placement of (T) beside the lower-left vertex (half_b). These entries have empty crop_ids so the main reader can make its own required adjudication crops. The raw 1er tokens in H are compared for their missing raised placement, not merely for LaTeX macro choice.

C alerts were covered: both raised er groups and Mme, ordinary capitals and the D of Deligne, doubled R, Hom/Ext/H underlines, both H exponents, live raised Ext i versus baseline condition i, both comparison signs, crossed membership, the apex low 2 and shift, prime on E, the detached top of the left E, quotation strokes, every prose doubt, and all five clipped marginal groups. Wholly agreed expressions are recorded in notation rather than added as no-change rows.

math_checks.statement: For i=0,1,2, determine which of the literal conditions 0=i≤2 and i∉[0,2] applies.

outcome.conclusion: The first condition applies only at i=0 among these three values; the second applies at none. Thus the literal displayed conditions do not specify the cases i=1,2. This small substitution check does not prove or refute the proposed triangle and was not used to replace the ink by ≤.
